sources.quote: Stress in Azerbaijani mostly falls on the final syllable of words except in some cases with imperative verbs and negative suffixes, where the stress falls on the first syllable (e.g. /d͡ʒæti/ 'bring', /d͡ʒetmæ/ 'don't go'). [Mokari & Werner 2017:211, section 'Prosodic features']

sources.citation: Essentials of Azerbaijani: An Introductory Course. University of Texas at Austin (Dept. of Slavic and Eurasian Studies), PDF dated 2006, 127 pp.; no author on title page.
sources.quote: 'The majority of words in Azerbaijani are stressed on the last syllable. In this course, for words or word forms where the stress is not on the final syllable, an accent mark will be written over the stressed vowel.' ... 'In most cases, the stress in an Azerbaijani word will shift to the final syllable of an added suffix' ... personal verbal suffixes of 'to be' 'are not stressed'; 'proféssor'-type loans keep non-final stress under suffixation.
sources.locator: PDF p.13, Introduction 'The Sounds of Azerbaijani'; also Unit 1 (plural suffix takes stress), Unit 2 'A note about stress' (copular personal suffixes unstressed), negative -mA shifts stress left
